headline: Core token proxies verified on Etherscan with resolved implementations; LiquidityPool implementation unresolvable this run; public repo and recognized-firm audits exist but last confirmed audit is >6 months stale relative to active development

findings.text: eETH proxy (0x35fA164735182de50811E8e2E824cFb9B6118ac2) is verified on Etherscan (abiSource=etherscan) and its implementation 0xCB3D917A965A70214f430a135154Cd5ADdA2ad84 was auto-resolved by the DeFiPunkd surfacer from Etherscan, indicating the implementation is also verified. weETH proxy (0xCd5fE23C85820F7B72D0926FC9b05b43E359b7ee) is similarly verified on Etherscan with implementation 0x2d10683E941275D502173053927AD6066e6aFd6B auto-resolved. LiquidityPool proxy (0x308861A430be4cce5502d0A12724771Fc6DaF216) is verified on Sourcify (verified=true) but returned proxy=null in the ABI API response due to Etherscan rate-limiting — its implementation address could not be confirmed as verified this run.

A public source repo exists at https://github.com/etherfi-protocol/smart-contracts (confirmed active, last updated Mar 24, 2026 per GitHub org page). The migration to a public repo occurred on 2024-02-15. No commit SHA was pinned this run (GitHub domain blocked for direct fetch); source-to-deployed-bytecode correspondence is therefore not confirmed.

Halborn conducted an audit covering EFIP-5, EFIP-8, and L2 Governance Token implementations (confirmed from Halborn case study page, dated approximately November 2024). Hats Finance ran an audit competition (report at GitHub, no pinned date this run). Certora has a formal verification fork (Certora/etherfi-smart-contracts-fork). The protocol's gitbook states audit reports are at https://github.com/etherfi-protocol/smart-contracts/tree/master/audits. No audit PDF URLs were provided in protocol.audit_links, and GitHub was inaccessible for direct fetch this run.

Halborn is a broadly recognized Solidity audit firm. Certora is recognized for formal verification. Hats Finance is a community audit competition platform (not in the tier-1 recognized firm list). The combination of Halborn + Certora coverage raises auditor recognition to credible.

The smart-contracts repo shows commit activity as recently as March 24, 2026 (per GitHub org page), approximately 16+ months after the last confirmed Halborn audit (~November 2024). Diff content was not sampled this run (GitHub inaccessible). Whether the LiquidityPool, eETH, or weETH implementation contracts were modified since the last audit scope is unknown.

eETH and weETH implementations are verified (resolved from Etherscan). LiquidityPool proxy is verified (Sourcify) but its implementation address was not resolved this run (proxy=null in ABI response), so implementation verification status for the fund-custody contract cannot be confirmed.

steelman.red: No audit PDFs are linked in the protocol manifest, the LiquidityPool implementation address could not be confirmed as verified, and the repo has been active for 16+ months since the last confirmed audit — a protocol holding billions of ETH with unconfirmed implementation verification and stale audit coverage could be orange-at-best.
steelman.orange: The two main fund-holding token contracts (eETH, weETH) have proxy and implementation both verified on Etherscan; a public repo with recent activity exists; recognized-firm audits (Halborn, Certora) are documented; but the LiquidityPool implementation verification is unconfirmed and last confirmed audit is >6 months old with active development — matching exactly the orange criteria for stale audit scope.
steelman.green: All surfaced proxies that could be checked are verified on Etherscan/Sourcify with implementations auto-resolved; a public source repo exists under etherfi-protocol; multiple recognized firms (Halborn, Certora) have audited the protocol; and no concrete evidence of material adverse drift was found this run.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: (1) the LiquidityPool proxy (the primary fund-custody contract) returned proxy=null in the ABI response, leaving its implementation's verification status unconfirmed this run — satisfying the 'proxy verified but implementation only partially verified' orange criterion; and (2) the last confirmed recognized-firm audit (Halborn, ~Nov 2024) is >6 months old relative to the analysis date of 2026-05-07, with the repo showing commit activity as recently as March 2026, and no later re-audit evidence was found this run — satisfying the 'audit scope is stale relative to deployment' orange criterion. Green requires ≤6 months of drift OR confirmed re-audit, neither of which was established.

protocol_metadata.about: ether.fi Stake is a liquid restaking protocol on Ethereum where users deposit ETH to receive eETH, a rebasing token representing their staked position, or weETH, a non-rebasing wrapped version. The protocol delegates validator operations to node operators while allowing stakers to retain control of their validator keys, and natively restakes deposited ETH on EigenLayer to earn additional AVS rewards. Core contracts (eETH, weETH, LiquidityPool) are UUPS-upgradeable proxies owned by a timelock at 0x9f26d4C.
